reviewed_api: Hardware type/config, version-0 attr extent and zero initialization, disabled leader and initially group-dependent member, pinned leader, no inheritance, exclude kernel/hypervisor, pid=0/cpu=-1 current-thread ownership and CLOEXEC.

Installed ioctl definitions and group flags; ID retrieval and the group read format nr/enabled/running/(value,id), reset changes counts but not cumulative scheduling times, pinned scheduling failure may yield EOF.
CLOEXEC ownership, partial-open cleanup and errno preservation. C uses installed syscall/ioctl symbols rather than handwritten numeric layouts.
findings: C read retries EINTR, checks exact byte count and exactly two unique matching IDs before copying output; EOF, short read and invalid identifiers fail rather than becoming a zero sample.

Rust repr(C) contains the same four ordered u64 fields and checks sizeof. FFI buffers are live and correctly sized. Two successful descriptors transfer to OwnedFd exactly once; failed opens close partial state.
PhantomData<Rc<()>> prevents moving or sharing the thread-owned group. The observed closures do not recursively enter the counter backend.

RAII disables the group on normal completion and unwind. A failed stop remains an observation error even if drop cleanup succeeds. Controls read the disabled state around an outside burn loop before any new reset/enable.
The body still executes when counter setup/read fails; snapshots, clock results and errors remain visible. Group failure is retained for that process.

A successful window allocates no error strings or observation vectors while counting. JSON conversion occurs after the group is disabled. Hardware includes clock/measurement instructions and generic wrapper code; separate empty windows expose only part of that overhead.
Before/after cumulative scheduling deltas and zero reset counts are checked independently by Rust and Python. No count scaling or empty-window subtraction is performed.

The runner freezes the same source path for three separately linked binaries, all original library hashes, compiler/RUSTFLAGS, reference headers and actual C header dependencies. All builds precede the fixed 18-process schedule.

The assessor verifies logs, actual binaries/object/headers, the unchanged fixture suffix, all witnesses, all 1152 raw windows, balanced order and complete six-pair eligibility. Invalid windows remain in raw evidence and disqualify the corresponding aggregate.
